_README: THE MONEY AND CALL RULES BOTH DASHBOARDS OBEY.
This file exists because the same question was being answered twice, in two
languages, in two repositories — and the two answers drifted apart four
separate times in a single evening (2026-08-18):
1. what counts as a sale       tracker said 'outcome typed on the day',
dashboard said 'money in Whop'
2. the deposit floor           tracker had $100, dashboard had $0
3. the same floor again        applied to Whop payments but not to money
typed into Collected On Call
4. what a payment proves       a payment was being read as proof that a
CALL HAD HAPPENED, not just that someone paid
Every one was found by a human noticing two screens disagreeing. That is not
a detection mechanism, it is luck.
TWO COPIES, ONE FILE. The Sales Command Center and the KPI dashboard deploy
independently, so each repository carries its own copy and neither can reach
the other at runtime. Copy this file WHOLE; never edit one side. Both repos
run `npm run check:rules`, which compares the two copies when they sit side
by side on a laptop and fails when they differ.
Changing a rule means: edit here, copy to the other repo, bump `version`,
run check:rules in both.

min_deposit.statement: A payment proves a sale once it reaches $100. Below that it is a token, and the deal stays whatever the closer recorded.
applies_to: money received through the payment processor
money taken during the call and typed into Collected On Call
min_deposit.why_flat_not_percentage: Under a percentage bar the same $500 deposit was a sale on a $2,000 deal and not one on a $4,000 deal, which judges the closer by the size of the offer rather than by what they actually banked.
min_deposit.source: [STATED - Moayad, chat 2026-08-18] 'even if a deposit doesnt pay the rest, its still technically a close unless its under $100 i think then that we shouldnt count as a close.'

what_a_payment_proves.statement: A payment proves a SALE. It does not prove that a CALL HAPPENED.
what_a_payment_proves.why: Everyone who arrives by the payment route is by definition a buyer, so counting them as a call held puts them on both sides of the close rate and can only push it up. Measured 2026-08-18 on Brey's August: 59.0% against the tracker's 48.6%, and the spread was almost entirely this.
a_call_happened_when: someone recorded an outcome for it (closed, deposit, or no_close)
a call for that person exists on the tracker AND its own outcome is not 'no show'
not_evidence_a_call_happened: a Calendly booking whose time has passed - Calendly is authoritative that a booking was MADE, but with no-shows going unmarked, counting those as held would assume a 100% show rate

refund.name: REFUND
refund.statement: A refunded deal is removed from revenue, from cash collected, and from the close rate — out of BOTH sides of it, not counted as a loss. The closer did close them; the customer later left, and scoring it as a failed call would make a different claim from the one the refund actually makes, on the closer's record.
refund.source: [STATED - Moayad, chat 2026-08-18] 'should be removed from revenue and cash collected, should also be removed from close rate.'
refund.cash_needs_no_rule: The processor reports a refund against the original payment, so refunded money nets to zero before it is ever read as cash. Verified against Whop on 2026-08-18: Vellatino Crawford, final_amount 2000, refunded_amount 2000, read as 0.
refund.outranks_the_arithmetic: Checked explicitly rather than left to fall out of a status list: a partly-refunded buyer would otherwise be put back by the paid-enough test. A REFUND on the tracker is a statement about the deal and beats what is left of their payments.

deal_value.statement: A deal is worth its recorded price, and never less than the cash actually received.
deal_value.why: A follow-up that later paid often carries no price at all, so reading the recorded price alone books a paid deal at zero. Where a price IS recorded and only part has been paid, the recorded price still wins - that is the deal value, and the remainder is what is outstanding.

source_of_truth.statement: Each fact comes from whoever owns it. Secondary sources fill a gap only when the answer is unambiguous.
